author: Isidorus Hispalensis

passages.original: 50. JUDAS LEBRÆUS, id est, corculus, hoc est, a corde, ipse est et Thadæus, ipse est Jutlas Jacobi, filii Josephi fratris Cleophe, et interpretatur confessor, in Mesopotamia, atque interioribus Ponti prædicavit. Sepultus est in Crito Armeniæ urbe, cujus festivitas vi Kalend. Novembris celebratur.
passages.english: 50. Judas Lebbaeus, that is, "little heart," that is, [named] from the heart, is also Thaddaeus; he is also Judas [son] of James, the son of Joseph the brother of Cleophas, and [his name] is interpreted "confessor." He preached in Mesopotamia and in the interior parts of Pontus. He was buried in Crito, a city of Armenia, and his feast is celebrated on the sixth day before the Kalends of November.
passages.notes: "Lebræus" is evidently a scanning error for Lebbaeus, and "Jutlas" for Judas. "Crito" is unidentified as given; other traditions name a different place. The genealogy (James son of Joseph, brother of Cleophas) is as the text states. The sixth day before the Kalends of November is 27 October.

passages.original: Ipse enim primus ecclesiam apud Alexandriam construxit, et in ea civitate primus prædicator et episcopus fuit. Qui et alio nomine idem Joannes nominatus fuit. Quem alii asserunt martyrio coronatum. Hieronymus autem eum affirmat in pace Ecclesiæ migrasse ad cœlum. Cujus depositio VII Kalend. Maii celebratur.
passages.english: For he first built a church at Alexandria, and in that city he was the first preacher and bishop. The same man was also called by another name, John. Some assert that he was crowned with martyrdom. Jerome, however, affirms that he passed to heaven in the peace of the Church. His deposition is celebrated on the seventh day before the Kalends of May.
passages.notes: The subject is Mark the Evangelist, from the preceding context. The identification with John reflects the conflation with John Mark. The seventh day before the Kalends of May is 25 April.
